common_name: Ankum's Pride Cranesbill (Dusky Pink-Magenta Bloody Geranium)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, poor to average soil in full sun; a bloody cranesbill selection holding the RHS Award of Garden Merit, grown for its dusky pink-magenta flowers over mounded, finely cut foliage.

directions: Ankum's Pride forms a dense, low mound of finely divided foliage covered through early summer in soft dusky-pink to magenta flowers, a touch muted compared to the vivid magenta of the straight species. Plant in full sun in average, well-drained soil; once established it tolerates heat and drought with no supplemental feeding. Shear lightly after the first flush to tidy the mound and often coax a second round of bloom.

common_name: Aviemore Cranesbill (Bright Carmine-Pink Bloody Geranium)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, poor to average soil in full sun; a bloody cranesbill selection with RHS Award of Garden Merit standing, valued for its bright carmine-pink flowers over a tidy mound.

directions: Aviemore produces a profusion of bright carmine-pink, saucer-shaped flowers over mounded, deeply cut foliage from late spring into summer. It thrives in lean, fast-draining soil in full sun and needs no winter protection in its hardiness range. Divide congested clumps in early spring every three to four years to keep flowering vigorous.

common_name: Little Bead Cranesbill (Dwarf Compact Bloody Geranium)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, poor to average soil in full sun to partial shade; an especially dwarf bloody cranesbill selection with RHS Award of Garden Merit standing, suited to rock gardens and troughs.

directions: Little Bead is a true miniature bloody cranesbill, forming a dense, button-like cushion of foliage only a few inches tall that is smothered in magenta-pink flowers in early summer. Its tiny scale makes it ideal for rock gardens, troughs, and the front edge of a sunny border, where larger sanguineum selections would swamp the space. Grow in lean, well-drained soil and avoid rich, wet sites that encourage floppy growth.

common_name: Splendens Striped Bloody Geranium (Enhanced Pale Pink Veined Cranesbill)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, poor to average soil in full sun to partial shade; an RHS Award of Garden Merit selection of the naturally striped var. striatum, with enhanced pink veining on a pale ground.

directions: Splendens refines the naturally occurring striped form of Geranium sanguineum var. striatum, bearing pale pink flowers finely penciled with darker rose veining on a compact, low mound. It prefers lean, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade and resents being crowded by taller neighbors. Deadhead spent flowers to extend the bloom period into midsummer.

common_name: White-ness Bigroot Geranium (White-Flowered Fragrant Groundcover Cranesbill)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained average to poor soil in partial to full shade; a white-flowered bigroot geranium selection holding the RHS Award of Garden Merit, grown as a durable, fragrant groundcover.

directions: White-ness carries pure white flowers above aromatic, semi-evergreen foliage that colors attractively in fall, spreading via thick rhizomes into a dense, weed-suppressing mat. Like other bigroot geraniums it tolerates dry shade, root competition from trees, and poor soil once established, making it a reliable underplanting for shrub borders and woodland edges. Cut back hard after flowering to refresh the foliage mat for the rest of the season.

common_name: Alba Grandiflora Garden Phlox (Large-Flowered Pure White Heirloom Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, organically rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, spacing generously for airflow; an old European garden phlox holding the RHS Award of Garden Merit for its large pure white flower trusses.

directions: Alba Grandiflora is a long-grown heirloom garden phlox valued for its unusually large, pure white florets held in dense, rounded trusses from midsummer into early fall. Give it moist, fertile, well-drained soil and generous spacing for airflow, since like most tall paniculata selections it is prone to powdery mildew in crowded or humid conditions. Divide every three to four years in early spring and deadhead before seed set to prevent muddy-colored seedlings from crowding out the named clone.

common_name: Danielle Garden Phlox (Clear White Mid-Season Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, organically rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, spacing generously for airflow; an RHS Award of Garden Merit garden phlox grown for its clear white flower trusses.

directions: Danielle bears clean white flower trusses on sturdy, upright stems through the middle of the summer border season. It performs best in moist, fertile, well-drained soil with good air circulation to reduce powdery mildew pressure common to tall garden phlox. Divide crowded clumps every few years in early spring to maintain vigor and flower size.

common_name: Eva Foerster Garden Phlox (Bicolor Pink and White Heirloom Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, organically rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, spacing generously for airflow; a classic European garden phlox with RHS Award of Garden Merit standing, grown for its pink-and-white bicolor flowers.

directions: Eva Foerster carries bicolor florets combining pink and white within the same truss, giving a softer, more variegated effect than solid-colored garden phlox cultivars. Plant in moist, fertile, well-drained soil with ample airflow between clumps to reduce mildew risk during humid summers. Divide every three to four years in early spring and remove spent flower heads before seed drops to keep the clump true to type.

common_name: Flamingo Garden Phlox (Bright Clear Pink Heirloom Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, organically rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, spacing generously for airflow; an RHS Award of Garden Merit garden phlox grown for its bright clear pink flower trusses.

directions: Flamingo produces bright, clear pink flower trusses that hold their color well through the heat of midsummer. It performs best in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with generous spacing to maintain airflow and reduce powdery mildew. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring to keep flowering strong.

common_name: Grey Lady Garden Phlox (Soft Lavender-Grey Heirloom Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, organically rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, spacing generously for airflow; an RHS Award of Garden Merit garden phlox grown for its unusual soft lavender-grey flower color.

directions: Grey Lady offers a subtle, smoky lavender-grey flower color that is unusual among garden phlox and pairs well with silver-leaved companions in the summer border. Grow in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with good air circulation between plants to limit powdery mildew. Divide every few years in early spring and deadhead to keep the display tidy and prevent off-color seedlings.

common_name: Le Mahdi Garden Phlox (Deep Violet-Blue Heirloom Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, organically rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, spacing generously for airflow; a long-grown French garden phlox with RHS Award of Garden Merit standing, noted for its deep violet-blue color, among the closest to true blue in the species.

directions: Le Mahdi is prized for flowers in a deep violet-blue shade, among the closest to true blue found in garden phlox, held in dense trusses on upright stems. It grows best in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with ample spacing for airflow to minimize powdery mildew. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring and deadhead before seed set.

common_name: Miss Mary Garden Phlox (Deep Pink Heirloom Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, organically rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, spacing generously for airflow; an RHS Award of Garden Merit garden phlox grown for its deep pink flower trusses.

directions: Miss Mary bears richly saturated deep pink flower trusses on compact, sturdy stems, making it useful toward the middle of the summer border. Grow in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with generous airflow between clumps to limit powdery mildew. Divide every three to four years in early spring and deadhead spent blooms to prolong the display.

common_name: Monica Lynden-Bell Garden Phlox (Pale Pink Heirloom Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, organically rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, spacing generously for airflow; an English-named garden phlox with RHS Award of Garden Merit standing, grown for its soft pale pink flower trusses.

directions: Monica Lynden-Bell carries soft, pale pink flowers in generous trusses on upright stems through the summer border season. It performs best in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with good airflow between plants to reduce the powdery mildew that affects crowded garden phlox. Divide every few years in early spring and deadhead to prevent seedlings diluting the named clone.

common_name: Mother of Pearl Garden Phlox (Pearl White Heirloom Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, organically rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, spacing generously for airflow; a classic garden phlox with RHS Award of Garden Merit standing, grown for its luminous pearl-white flowers.

directions: Mother of Pearl bears luminous pearl-white flowers with the faintest blush, held in large, dense trusses that glow in evening light. Grow in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with ample spacing to maintain airflow and reduce powdery mildew pressure. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring to sustain strong flowering.

common_name: Prince of Orange Garden Phlox (Orange-Red Heirloom Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, organically rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, spacing generously for airflow; an RHS Award of Garden Merit garden phlox grown for its vivid orange-red flower color, rare among paniculata cultivars.

directions: Prince of Orange stands out among garden phlox for its vivid orange-red flower color, a shade rarely seen in the species and useful for hot-color border schemes. It performs best in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with generous spacing for airflow to limit powdery mildew. Divide every three to four years in early spring and remove spent blooms before they set seed.

common_name: Prospero Garden Phlox (Lilac and White Bicolor Heirloom Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, organically rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, spacing generously for airflow; a Dutch-raised garden phlox with RHS Award of Garden Merit standing, grown for its lilac-and-white bicolor flowers.

directions: Prospero bears pale lilac flowers with a lighter, almost white center, giving each floret a soft bicolor effect in large summer trusses. Grow in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with good airflow between plants to reduce powdery mildew in humid weather. Divide every three to four years in early spring and deadhead to keep the clump vigorous.

common_name: Rosa Pastell Garden Phlox (Pale Rose-Pink Heirloom Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, organically rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, spacing generously for airflow; a German-raised garden phlox with RHS Award of Garden Merit standing, grown for its pale rose-pink flower trusses.

directions: Rosa Pastell carries soft, pale rose-pink flowers in airy trusses that blend easily with both hot and cool color schemes in the summer border. It grows best in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with ample spacing between clumps to promote airflow and reduce powdery mildew. Divide every three to four years in early spring to keep the planting floriferous.

common_name: Uspekh Garden Phlox (Violet and White Bicolor Heirloom Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, organically rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, spacing generously for airflow; a Russian-raised garden phlox (the name means 'success') with RHS Award of Garden Merit standing, grown for its violet-and-white bicolor flowers.

directions: Uspekh bears violet-purple florets with a contrasting lighter center, giving each flower a star-like bicolor pattern within dense summer trusses. Grow in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with good airflow between plants to limit powdery mildew in humid conditions. Divide every three to four years in early spring and deadhead before seed set to preserve the named clone.

common_name: Velvet Flame Garden Phlox (Purple and White Bicolor Heirloom Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, organically rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, spacing generously for airflow; an RHS Award of Garden Merit garden phlox grown for its rich purple-and-white bicolor flowers.

directions: Velvet Flame bears rich purple florets with a contrasting white eye, lending a lively bicolor effect to its dense summer trusses. Grow in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with ample airflow between clumps to reduce powdery mildew in humid weather. Divide every three to four years in early spring and deadhead spent blooms to prolong the display.

common_name: Visions Garden Phlox (Pale to Medium Pink Heirloom Phlox)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, organically rich, well-drained soil in full sun to light afternoon shade, spacing generously for airflow; an RHS Award of Garden Merit garden phlox grown for its pale-to-medium pink flower trusses.

directions: Visions bears flowers that shift from pale to medium pink across the truss as they age, giving a softly shaded effect uncommon among garden phlox cultivars. Plant in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with generous spacing for airflow to limit powdery mildew. Divide every three to four years in early spring to keep the clump blooming well.
